raw_response:
I farm the way I know best: I keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 20 mu, my well water, and my family labor. At my age, with many years in the field and some family members working off-farm, I do not want a plan that is too scattered or too risky. I will keep a smaller part in cotton because I already grow it and it helps me spread risk, but I will not let cotton take too much land because it needs more watching and hand work. On the wheat-maize land, I will use better seed and put fertilizer where it gives me stable output. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in my area depends heavily on timely water, especially if I want a safe harvest. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep management simpler after wheat harvest so I can move fast in the busy season. For cotton, I will keep the area moderate, use improved seed, irrigate when needed from the well, and control pests carefully because cotton can lose yield quickly if insects get ahead of me. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, saves labor, and is easier for me to manage across the year.
